method_function.text: 界定源无关连贯性构念及其测量边界。

facts.statement: 人工收集100本新近出版书，约平衡所列题材并含线性/非线性叙事，购买电子版；平均190K tokens（BookSum112K）。作者未找到完整在线摘要但找到书评，并承认近期模型仍可能见过原书；不将此当作已证明无污染。

method_function.text: 用新近材料降低摘要记忆混淆，保留剩余暴露风险。

facts.statement: 从epub提取全部文本元素，不另做自动清洗以保留视觉分隔；章节等非叙事内容可能进入摘要。把书分成不重叠且在句界结束的块，块长C小于模型窗口W。

method_function.text: 确定输入预处理及共同分块操作。

facts.statement: 比较同100本书的层级合并与增量更新；主表跨五种既有instruction-tuned LLM及Claude两种块长配置。人工错误标注、precision再验证、成对偏好评价是同语料的不同测量程序，不把句子或每次API调用当独立实验。

method_function.text: 区分书/摘要/句子/错误标注和共享测量单位。

facts.statement: 层级流程先逐块生成最低层摘要，再每次合并尽可能多的连续摘要并加入同层前序已合并摘要作上下文；合并提示、摘要和前序上下文总长须低于W−G_l；递归直到全书剩一个摘要。

method_function.text: 实现带前序上下文的多层合并。

facts.statement: 增量流程以第一块摘要初始化global summary；此后每次把下一块和当前摘要送入更新提示，超Gn则另调用压缩提示。层级摘要超限则重生成至固定次数，不另外采用增量式压缩；重试上限未在PDF给出。

method_function.text: 实现依次更新及超长处理，区分两策略控制流。

facts.statement: 一般摘要/更新/合并提示要求关键事件、背景、角色动机、首次引入实体及一致时间顺序；压缩提示按word budget删除不重要信息。附录提供这些提示，Llama用简化版；Gn与报告长度之外，提示具体按words表述，不擅自建立words到tokens转换。

method_function.text: 明确提示操纵和文本长度约束。

facts.statement: 除Llama外，用GPT4后处理移除渐进生成措辞及目录/致谢/作者简介等非叙事信息，提示要求其余不改；Llama则在末个标点截断并用字符串匹配去掉复制的提示句，不使用会提升其连贯性的GPT4重写清理。

method_function.text: 记录实际生成后清理和模型特定例外。

facts.statement: 使用现成Together Llama-2-7B-32K-Instruct（既有BookSum长摘要微调）、Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1，Azure gpt-4 2023-03-15/gpt-3.5-turbo-0301及2023年9月Claude2 API；Llama实际窗口4096。本文流程为zero-shot提示，无本文新增微调。

method_function.text: 交代模型获取方式与既有训练来源，不误作作者训练。

facts.statement: 主比较默认块长2048、Gn900、温度0.5、p=1 ancestral sampling；Claude默认温度1，压缩温度1。另比较Claude块长88000；Llama不能完成增量更新所以无其增量结果。

method_function.text: 固定生成设置并记录缺失配置原因。

facts.statement: 四名有英语校对经验的Upwork标注者读摘要、标全部confusing spans并提出澄清问题，允许双span关系；GPT4块4096/Gn1200摘要共1193错误（增量840/层级353）。文称每人25 disjoint summaries及总成本$3000/$15每摘要，两策略总分配口径未完全闭合，保留文字而不补人数×书×摘要推算。

method_function.text: 实施细粒度人工错误发现并保留分母分配歧义。

facts.statement: 收集span/问题后人工归为八类：实体遗漏、事件遗漏、因果遗漏、叙事不连续、不重要细节、语言、内在矛盾、重复；taxonomy由GPT4错误归纳而非先给SNaC模板。表1比例为错误出现次数除所有摘要总句数，非错误类型在全部错误中的占比。

method_function.text: 定义错误标签及每句发生率分母。

facts.statement: 再验证让同四人评原先未标的25本书，混合并隐藏人工/GPT4标注来源；对1659条span-question判断agree/partially agree/disagree，题问须相关、摘要别处不能解答且影响主线。precision将agree和partial全部算接受，即span有混淆但题问未达标也计入。

method_function.text: 明确人工精度核验、盲化与宽松接受阈值。

facts.statement: 验证得人工标注precision79.7%、GPT4标注78.2%；未收集每摘要重叠全量标注，因此没有验证召回。第二验证任务数周后才通知并付每摘要$1.7+每标注$.15，不能据此推导独立新标注人员。

method_function.text: 区分精度验证和未实施召回/一致性测量。

facts.statement: 自动评价用GPT4 few-shot，每句分别输入完整摘要、目标句、八类错误定义，要求对不能由摘要自身解除且显著影响主线的混淆输出澄清问题/类型，否则No confusion；使用两份完整示例摘要和42条句标注。PDF M4明确缩略，未包含完整42条。

method_function.text: 记录实际LLM裁判提示和逐句调用接口。

facts.statement: 单摘要BooookScore是其n个句子中GPT4返回No confusion的比例（式1），一句多个问题仍算一个confusion单位；系统分数为每份摘要该比例的平均，非按全部句子合池加权。人工版本将连续多句span及span关系当单个‘句子’以调整不同标注单位。

method_function.text: 明确二层平均、无混淆二值计分及人工单位调整。

facts.statement: 用人工标注替代式1裁判输出，增量/层级得82.1/89.4，对应同4096设置GPT4标注82.4/90.8；类型发生率图显示GPT4偏标遗漏、较少重复/语言。作者没有进一步验证类型准确性；不是报告类型相关系数或全面分类效度。

method_function.text: 验证系统均分接近并识别类型层面的不一致。

facts.statement: 表2按配置报告平均BooookScore、tiktoken长度、相对源的新三元组比例和摘要内重复三元组比例。GPT4层级/增量89.1/82.5；Claude2048为91.1/78.6，88000为90.3/90.9；Llama层级72.4且重复36.1%。未给三元组重复分子是distinct还是occurrence的完整实现。

method_function.text: 比较连贯性与输出长度/重复，保留实际文本统计定义边界。

facts.statement: 同四名标注者各比较25对（共100对）GPT4增量/层级摘要；随机打乱两策略展示次序并隐藏方法名，允许tie，分别评整体、细节、结构节奏、逻辑易懂。此偏好任务与细粒度错误标注共享人员而非独立样本证据。

method_function.text: 实施成对偏好与次序/方法标签控制。

facts.statement: 100对偏好中增量/层级/tie：整体44/54/2、细节83/11/6、结构35/59/6、逻辑38/53/9。高coherence并非偏好全部维度优势；只是观察到偏好率，不补显著性检验。

method_function.text: 报告成对选择的各维度计数比例并保留ties。

facts.statement: 对GPT4增量2048的100摘要画BooookScore对token长度散点，文字称无可辨相关；未报Pearson/Spearman系数或检验。

method_function.text: 用散点探索长度与评分关系，区别视觉判断与已做统计估计。

facts.statement: 对上述100摘要分数进行1000次有放回、样本量100的bootstrap，文称计算样本mean并报告SD=.015作为稳定性证据；未给CI/置信水平，文字对1000 samples聚合表述简略。

method_function.text: 记录已实施重采样稳定性分析及报告限制。

facts.statement: 附录用SQuALITY验证集4–6K词科幻短篇：GPT4一次性摘要基线，超窗口截源；增量块256/512。表5仅报告ROUGE-L14.9/13.2/13.7，BooookScore留待新版，不因引言提hierarchical就补该条件结果。

method_function.text: 区分辅助短文参考摘要检验与主书长任务。

facts.statement: 附录对所有层级摘要计算BLANC与SUPERT：BLANC测给定摘要是否帮助既有模型填源文mask，SUPERT为摘要与从源构建伪参考的语义相似；给出配置得分但未给本论文mask方案、伪参考选择、具体编码器等完整实现。主实验未算ROUGE，不排除辅助SQuALITY实际ROUGE-L。

method_function.text: 保留实际替代指标与专用实现未知，不以指标名补算法。

An evaluation framework for book-length summarization. Since we lack gold summaries, we
design our evaluation framework to be reference-free, which aids in scalability. To do this, our evaluation framework synthesizes best-practices of prior document understanding and summarization
evaluation research. Our evaluation employs: (1) fine-grained evaluation units as recommended by
LongEval (Krishna et al., 2023); (2) information-seeking questions to represent naturally-occurring
points of confusion (Ko et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2023; Meng et al., 2023; Newman et al., 2023);
and (3) focus on summary coherence, which evaluates the logical structure and readability of the
summary itself (Goyal et al., 2022a). We do not directly evaluate the faithfulness of the summaries
(i.e., how factually accurate they are at conveying information from the source text), as the length of
the source texts poses considerable issues for any existing faithfulness evaluation. We qualitatively
discuss faithfulness in Section 5 and leave further investigation for future work.

Collecting a corpus of newly-published books. The only existing public dataset for book-length
summarization is BookSum (Kryscinski et al., 2022), which contains famous books from the Project
Gutenberg public-domain repository along with reference summaries scraped from popular websites
such as CliffNotes and GradeSaver. Both the source books and reference summaries are in the
pretraining data of existing LLMs: Chang et al. (2023) confirm that many books in the BookSum
held-out split (e.g., The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, The Picture of Dorian Gray) are among the
most-memorized books by GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-Turbo, and we were able to auto-complete several
reference BookSum summaries by prompting GPT-4 with a short prefix of the summary.
To reduce the confounding impact of summary memorization, we manually collect 100 books3 published within the past year to form our dataset (see Table 3 for a full list). Some of these books
could still have appeared in the pretraining dataset of recent LLMs such as Claude 2 and LLaMa2,
although it is much less likely than in BookSum. However, summaries of these books do not publicly exist: we did not find summaries online for any books in our dataset, which significantly lowers
the possibility of LLM memorization.4 The average length of the books in our dataset is 190K tokens, compared to 112K tokens in BookSum. Due to copyright laws, we cannot publicly release this
dataset; even if we could, we would still recommend that researchers collect their own datasets of
newly-published books to minimize contamination with LLMs of the future.

3
We roughly balance our dataset across the following genres: fiction, non-fiction, sci-fi, fantasy, historical,
contemporary, and memoir. We also include both linear and non-linear (multi-perspective and time-shifting)
narratives in the dataset, and we purchase electronic copies of each of the 100 books in the dataset.

However, we did find book reviews, which intentionally do not reveal major plot points or other spoilers.

Hierarchical merging works as follows:
1. Obtain summaries at the base level l = 0 by summarizing each chunk.
2. Obtain summaries for the first level l = 1 by prompting the LLM to merge as many consecutive level-0 summaries si , si+1 , . . . as possible17 such that the total length of the merging
prompt, the selected summaries, and the prior context (if there exists a preceding summary
at the same level) is less than W − Gl , where Gl is a hyperparameter controlling summary
length that varies depending on the level l.
3. Repeat the previous step recursively until we are left with a single summary for the book.

A.2.1

C OMPRESSION

The compression step is required for incremental updating. Through our experimentation, we have
observed that as the model processes a book through incremental updating, it consistently adds more
information to the running summary instead of removing things. Even with an updating prompt, the
summary often surpasses the target length as removing content from it is not in the model’s natural
inclination. Thus, a separate prompt is needed for the model to condense the summary. However,
in hierarchical summarization, condensing is not required. The merging step is less likely to run
over the summary limit since it does not have to work with a pre-existing running summary. If
the summaries generated during hierarchical merging go over the summary limit, simply asking the
model to regenerate up to a fixed number of times would suffice.

Hierarchical merging: Wu et al. (2021) propose a method in which an LLM (in their case, GPT3) is fine-tuned via reinforcement learning to summarize each chunk and then hierarchically merge
the chunk-level summaries until one summary is left of the entire input document. This method
has since been simplified into a zero-shot prompting strategy without further training, as shown in
Figure 1 (left). Hierarchical merging requires three unique prompts for (1) summarizing an input
chunk, (2) merging chunk-level summaries, and (3) merging summaries with added context from
previously-generated merged summaries. We ensure that the total length of each prompt and its
associated inputs is less than W − Gl , where Gl is a hyperparameter controlling summary length
that varies depending on the level l. Summaries are recursively merged until only one summary (of
the full book) remains; see Appendix A.1 for further details.

We investigate how well existing reference-free evaluation metrics work for our setting where the
source text is at book level. BLANC (Vasilyev et al., 2020) measures how helpful a summary is
to understanding the source document by testing if a pre-trained model can better fill in masked

between the a summary and some pseudo reference summaries generated from the source document.
We compute both metrics for hierarchical summaries generated under all configurations, and show
results in Table 7. Both BLANC and SUPERT differ by nearly negligible margins across models,
which makes them less meaningful. Furthermore, both metrics rate Claude 2 (88000) summaries
as inferior to GPT-3.5-Turbo (2048) summaries, a finding that clearly contradicts results from our
qualitative analysis.

Our error taxonomy is derived just from errors made by GPT-4. We decided to conduct our
human evaluations in Section 3 on summaries produced by GPT-4 for two reasons: (1) we wanted
our error taxonomy to focus on errors that are actually made by state-of-the-art LLMs (unlike e.g.,
fluency errors present in SNaC); and (2) human evaluation is very costly, so we could not evaluate
many different LLMs on our annotation budget. Similarly, we implement B OOOOK S CORE using
GPT-4 as a base LLM, which may have some systematic biases that could be alleviated by using a
pool of LLM annotators as in AlpacaEval (Dubois et al., 2023).

B OOOOK S CORE can be expensive to run. Since computing B OOOOK S CORE requires iterating
through a summary sentence by sentence using GPT-4, it can be expensive and slow especially given
that the annotation prompt is long (see Appendix M.4). We did experiment with an approach that
asked GPT-4 to annotate errors in the entire summary at once, but the generated annotations would
often include too many trivial questions, and alignment with human judgments was low. That said,
despite the API costs of GPT-4 and the relatively slow time to evaluate one summary, B OOOOK S CORE
is still significant cheaper and faster than performing human evaluations.
B OOOOK S CORE does not account for the relative importance of different error types. Unlike
similar evaluation frameworks such as MQM (Freitag et al., 2021), we choose not to assign severity
weights to different error types. Nowadays, powerful LLMs rarely make errors related to grammar,
which can be objectively defined. For other error types like those in our taxonomy, the notion of
assigning relative importance is ill-defined. Furthermore, prior work (Goyal et al., 2022a; Dou et al.,
2022) shows low recall between human annotations for NLG evaluation, which indicates that error
type severity is subjective as annotators often do not highlight issues that others may find critical.
No validation of recall. Due to the expense, we do not collect overlapping annotations for each
summary during human evaluation. Since the annotation task involves subjectivity, overlapping
annotations can help ensure that all errors within a summary can be captured. However, recent
work (Krishna et al., 2023) shows that a comprehensive annotation of all information units is not
required to produce a useful aggregate score that can be used to rank different models.

Given a book summary and a sentence from that summary, determine if that sentence causes any confusion. Types of confusion include the following:

- Entity omission: an entity, real or abstract (person, object, place, concept, etc.) is mentioned, but key details are missing or unclear
- Event omission: an event is mentioned, but key details are missing or unclear
- Causal omission: the reason or motivation for something is missing or unclear
- Salience: inclusion of trivial details that do not contribute to the main storyline
- Discontinuity: an interruption in the flow of the narrative, including but not restricted to: sudden jumps between perspectives, time periods, or settings; poor transition between sentences or paragraphs; sentences or paragraphs that seem out of place; illogical sentence order or summary structure
- Duplication: redundant repetition of similar information
- Inconsistency: two parts of the summary contain contradicting information
- Language: grammar issues; confusing wording or phrasing; etc.

For something to qualify as a confusion, it must meet these two conditions:

1. Without resolving the confusion, readers would struggle substantially to grasp the main narrative, or the summary would appear incoherent.
2. The confusion can't be resolved solely using the information provided in the summary.

If the given sentence involves confusion that meets these two qualifications, ask relevant clarifying questions and provide the confusion types. There can be multiple questions, and keep in mind that a sentence may involve multiple types of confusion. If the given sentence doesn't involve any confusion, simply say "no confusion".
